qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Operating density across dispersed homes provides localized maintenance efficiencies, but fails to generate economic returns above capital cost. 5-year median ROIC of ~4.5-4.8% is far below the 12% hurdle. Extreme competition from millions of mom-and-pop landlords and apartments caps pricing power, while the FTC's 2024 $48M deceptive junk-fee settlement highlights regulatory resistance to fee-based extraction.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 4.8%, REJECT). Single-family rental REIT model is asset-heavy with structural ROIC of ~4.5-4.8%, far below the 12% threshold. Local market operating density cannot overcome high tenant substitution from fragmented mom-and-pop rentals, while the 2024 FTC deceptive pricing/junk-fee settlement underscores severe regulatory friction on institutional landlord fee practices.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median ROIC is 4.8% (4.2%-4.7% in FY2024-2025), well below the 12% hurdle. Total debt stands at ~$8.0-8.5B with Debt/EBITDA of ~5.8-6.1x. In September 2024, the FTC finalized a $48M settlement against Invitation Homes for deceptive undisclosed junk fees (mandatory smart home/utility fees) and unfair eviction/deposit withholding practices, demonstrating that pricing power is constrained and subject to intense federal and local regulatory backlash.
